timeline.text: PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim–Real Benchmark for Evaluating GPT-6 Astra in Physical Interaction.
Two research questions. Q1: How Well Does GPT-6 Astra Perform in Contact-Rich Manipulation? Q2: Can Simulation Reliably Reflect Its Real-World Performance?
L1: Selection & alignment. Establish the right contact. Align before placement. Marker Placement. Success rate across 5 L1 tasks: Simulation 66.7%, Real World 80.0%.
L2: Add force regulation. Maintain contact. Regulate force while moving. Whiteboard Wiping. Success rate across 7 L2 tasks: Simulation 47.6%, Real World 47.6%.
L3: Add contact reconfiguration. Reconfigure contacts. Coordinate sustained interaction. Nut Removal. Success rate across 4 L3 tasks: 0% in both environments.
Success rates decline as interaction demands increase. No L3 task was completed in either environment. Task-weighted success; 3 trials per task per environment.
Q2: Can Simulation Reliably Reflect Its Real-World Performance? Physically Matched. Visually Matched. Same Robot Platform. Shared Task Goals & Success Criteria.
Visually Matched: Layout & Appearance. Camera Views. Simulation and Real World.
Physically Matched: Geometry & Mass. Contact Response. Jelly measured mass: 26.4 g. Marker length: 150 mm. Compare responses under contact.
10 / 16 Tasks with Matching Success Counts. The other 6 differ by one successful trial. 3 trials per task per environment. Each tile: Simulation · Real World.
Similar Interaction Bottlenecks. Hat Hanging — Alignment. The hat is lifted but not hung.
Similar Interaction Bottlenecks. Jelly Handling — Contact–Force Coordination. The gripper closes, but the jelly stays on the surface.
For GPT-6 Astra, Matched Simulation Reflects Key Real-World Strengths and Limits. PhysLadder. physladder-benchmark.com
